cards.caveat: Only the completion subset (a small share of tests) supports d-squared scaling; burn time of extinguished droplets is cut short and must not be read without the end-of-test flag. In the CFI data (PSI-39, DOI 10.60555/m6pj-a914) the hot-flame burn time vs d0 slope is reversed (-1.42, from group_effects_numbers.json): large droplets reach radiative extinction earlier.
cards.equipment_implication: Droplet-combustion sizing or burn-time planning must condition on completion vs extinction; do not extrapolate a single d-squared law across both outcomes.
cards.finding: For FLEX droplets that burned to completion, log burn time rises with log initial diameter with slope 2.13 (95% CI 1.76 to 2.52, n=27), close to the d-squared value of 2. Over all tests the slope drops to 1.31 (n=260) and for tests ending in extinction to 1.00 (n=179).
cards.title: FLEX droplets: burn time follows the d-squared law only when the burn completes

cards.caveat: The EDA report (section 6.1) states there is no hot ignition at ~21% O2 for butane/propane; this is not reproduced by the Feature Store rows (hot_ignition_raw), so the card reports the measured rate. Small n, mixed fuel fractions and pressures, test-day effects are strong; flames that ignite mostly self-extinguish (SE). PSI-10 (Flame Design) rows carry no outcome column and are not used.
cards.equipment_implication: Do not assume a cabin-air (~21% O2) flame will fail to ignite: treat ignition as possible but uncertain and keep ignition sources controlled in the habitat.
cards.finding: At 20.5-21.5% initial O2 (butane and propane, ACME CFI-G normal flames) 20 of 34 tests hot-ignited (rate 0.59; butane 5/11, propane 15/23). At 35% O2 and above the rate is 0.72 (n=86).
cards.title: ACME normal flames: hot ignition at about 21% O2 is partial, not absent

cards.caveat: Smoke rows (SAME and SAME-R flight data) sit in the PSI-101 workbook; the pooled n includes 10 ground rows whose column mapping is unverified (the within-material check is flight only). Correlation, not a causal model; materials are not balanced across campaigns.
cards.equipment_implication: Smoke-detector or particle-size models must include material as a feature; without it the learned heater-temperature trend points the wrong way.
cards.finding: Across all smoke tests, heater temperature ratio Rt/R0 correlates negatively with particle mean diameter (Spearman rho -0.27, n=141); with material held fixed the partial rho is 0.49, and within each material it is positive in 5 of 5 materials.
cards.title: Smoke particle size: Simpson's paradox hides the heater-temperature effect

cards.caveat: PMMA only, burns with an O2 drop larger than 0.2 points; O2 and CO2 changes carry nearly the same information, so they are not independent targets. Median ratio, not a fit uncertainty.
cards.equipment_implication: O2 and CO2 sensors in the enclosure cross-check each other; a ratio far from about -0.8 for a PMMA-like fuel signals a sensor fault.
cards.finding: Median change in CO2 over change in O2 for PMMA burns is -0.80 (n=66), against the theoretical -0.83 (-5/6).
cards.title: BASS-II PMMA: CO2 gain per O2 lost matches stoichiometry
